[element-pub-id]
=== `<pub-id>` Publication Identifier (in a citation)

In a bibliographic citation (<<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>> or <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>) or a citation to a related object (<<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>), this element names an identifier of the cited publication.

#### Usage/Remarks
##### Custom Publication Identifier Type (<<attribute-pub-id-type,`@pub-id-type`>>)

The <<attribute-pub-id-type,`@pub-id-type`>> attribute can be used to preserve information concerning the type of contributors being cited (for example, “`doi`”s, “`pmid`”s, or “`ark`”s). <<attribute-pub-id-type,`@pub-id-type`>> has as its values a fixed list of types. If your identifier type is not one of the listed types, you can use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to describe the actual type. Set the value of <<attribute-pub-id-type,`@pub-id-type`>> to “`custom`” and also use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to hold any identifier type you require. For example:
[source,xml]
....
<pub-id pub-id-type="custom"  
     custom-type="matlab"...>...</pub-id>
....

#### Tagged Sample

##### For Digital Object Identifier (DOI)
[source,xml]
....
...
<ref>
 <mixed-citation publication-type="data">Xu, J. <etal/> 
  <data-title>Cross-platform ultradeep transcriptomic profiling 
   of human reference RNA samples by RNA-Seq</data-title>. 
  <source>Sci. Data</source> 
  <volume>1</volume>:<elocation-id>140020</elocation-id> 
  doi: <pub-id pub-id-type="doi">10.1038/sdata.2014.20</pub-id> 
  (<year iso-8601-date="2014">2014</year>).</mixed-citation>
</ref>
...
....
